message.content: I read the full morning feed before acting. The feed contained nothing material: AAPL drifted in a narrow band from about $221.84 at the open down to roughly $220.5 by 09:57, and every headline was either the boilerplate "shares little changed in early trade" or a repeated restatement of the same sell-side consensus number ("FY25 EPS $8.40," recycled by five different outlets). That $8.40 is an analyst estimate, not a company-reported figure, so I did not treat it as a basis for the decision. Instead I pulled AAPL's fiscal 2024 10-K figures (filed 2024-11-01): revenue $391.0B, net income $93.7B, diluted EPS $6.08, and operating cash flow $118.3B — a business still generating very large, high-quality cash flow, with no negative news in the tape. The live quote moved up to $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), i.e. price had recovered above the morning's range, so I bought a modest starter position well inside the mandate: 30 shares of AAPL with a limit of $222.90 (about 0.08% above the ask, effectively at market), which filled at $222.90 for roughly $6,687 — under the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, leaving ample cash in the account and moving no money out. I deliberately kept the size small because the session's information content was essentially nil and the price is not cheap at about 36.6× trailing EPS of $6.08, keeping room to add on weakness or to use the remaining daily budget on MSFT if a real catalyst appears.
message.reasoning_content:
Order filled at 222.90, 30 shares = $6,687. Under $10k/order and under $20k total today.
